project: Preserve Plan-Parallel Executor Results at Merge
description: Fix the @you/plan-parallel fan-in path so the merger receives the original request and every completed executor result exactly once, with deterministic regression evidence, a documented root cause, a narrowly scoped correction, and delivery through actual PR merge.

context.customerAsk: A recorded @you/plan-parallel run completed 10 executor children, but merge-plan-results received no usable delegated outputs and claimed that no child results existed. Reproduce the failure with known mock executor outputs, locate whether the loss occurs during result collection, join payload movement, or merger prompt assembly, fix it, retain the failing scenario as regression coverage, and document the before/after evidence and root cause in the PR description.
context.problem: Successful child execution does not currently guarantee successful fan-in. The merger can start and complete without completed planned-task results in its rendered input, silently discarding executor work and returning a misleading, useless primary result.
context.solution: Add a deterministic N-child plan-parallel functional scenario that captures the merger's actual input, use it to identify the precise result-loss mechanism, and correct only the owning collection, routing, or prompt-input behavior so the original request and every eligible completed child result reach the merger exactly once. Preserve the regression, focused lower-layer proof, and before/after evidence.

acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic plan-parallel functional scenario runs N executor children with unique known outputs and proves that the merger's rendered input contains the original request and all N outputs exactly once.
The regression test is demonstrated failing on current main and passing after the fix, with the red output, green output, and exact root-cause mechanism recorded in the PR description.

Completed child results remain associated with the correct generated Work and are not lost, duplicated, replaced by task specifications, or reordered in a way that violates the Factory's deterministic input contract.
Existing plan-parallel functional coverage and focused Factory Session/Work routing coverage remain green, and any new package-level tests follow the post-PR #1862 split test layout.

The implementation stays within the identified fan-in result-routing, collection, or packaged Factory wiring fault surface and preserves explicit state, isolated side effects, service ownership, and existing public contracts.
Typecheck passes; tests pass; there are no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Reproduce and localize missing merger inputs
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a deterministic plan-parallel run with recognizable child results so that I can observe exactly where successful executor outputs disappear before merger execution.
acceptanceCriteria: A functional test runs the plan-parallel behavior with N greater than one deterministic executor results whose unique strings can be distinguished from planner task payloads and from the original request.

The test inspects the merger dispatch through the normal application execution path and asserts that its rendered input contains the original request and every unique completed child result exactly once.
On current main, the test fails for the recorded missing-output behavior, and the PR description includes the relevant red test output without weakening the assertion to match the bug.

The investigation identifies whether loss occurs in result collection, relationship/join routing, or merger input/prompt assembly and records the exact mechanism and owning boundary in the PR description.
The test uses deterministic edge replacement and observation rather than sleeps, live providers, or an alternate application composition path.
Any package-level regression coverage under pkg/services/factory_sessions/internal/execution is placed in the post-PR #1862 split test layout rather than recreating the former large test file.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass, except for the intentionally captured pre-fix red run on current main
userStories.notes: Added a root.BuildProcess/Process.Execute functional regression with 10 independent planned-task children, deterministic per-child executor markers, exact-once parent/result assertions, Work-name/result association checks, and planner-payload substitution checks. The same focused test passes repeatedly on the current origin/main, so the PRD's required current-main red reproduction is not yet established. History localizes the previously observed omission to packaged merger prompt assembly: before b0bf1dd597 the merger body did not render Factory inputs; the current base already contains that prompt block and its Payload/PreviousOutput/Content fallback. Keep this story incomplete until the recorded failing scenario is reproduced or the remaining result-loss mechanism is proven.

userStories.title: Deliver every completed child result to the merger
userStories.description: As a plan-parallel customer, I want the merger to receive every successful executor's result so that the final response faithfully synthesizes the work I paid the Factory to perform.
acceptanceCriteria: After the fix, the deterministic regression proves the merger input contains the original parent request and all N unique completed child results exactly once.
The merger receives completed result content rather than only the executor's assigned task payload, and each result remains traceable to the correct child Work identity.
The fix preserves existing all-children completion gating: the merger does not run early, failed-child behavior is not reclassified, and unrelated Factory routing remains unchanged.
Focused tests at the owning lower layer directly prove the corrected collection or prompt-input invariant, while the functional test proves the full packaged plan-parallel behavior.
The PR description records the exact root cause plus the same regression command's before-fix failure and after-fix success evidence.
Existing plan-parallel functional suites pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
